title: Week 6
priceNote: Prices are estimates from typical Aldi and Publix shelf prices and do not include tax. Christmas week: Sunday's mojo pork covers nine meals, Christmas Eve is a 15-minute sheet pan and Christmas dinner for two is this week's new one.
allergyNote: Nothing on this plan contains tree nuts or fish. The mojo marinade is homemade, so there is nothing hidden in it. Holiday cookies, candy and stuffing from other people often contain tree nuts, so ask before you eat them.
weekendNote: Christmas weekend. Nothing is required. A portion of cranberry chicken with couscous is waiting for Saturday's lunch.
snacks: Cottage cheese with a drizzle of honey

mon.heads: Everything today comes from Sunday's prep. Dinner makes Wednesday's lunch.

tue.heads: Tonight's soup takes 20 minutes after pickleball and covers Thursday and Friday lunches.

wed.heads: Tonight, move the frozen pork portion to the fridge for Christmas Eve nachos.

thu.heads: Christmas Eve. Dinner is a 15-minute sheet pan after pickleball.

fri.heads: Merry Christmas. Dinner for two is this week's new one, and it makes Saturday's lunch.

prep.title: Sunday batch prep
prep.makes: About 9 portions of mojo pork, 2 trays of roasted roots, lime rice and beans, chipotle crema, pickled onions, a breakfast bake, 2 jars of oats, 6 eggs
steps: Start the mojo pork in the crock pot first thing (low 8 hours or high 5).
Heat the oven to 425°F. Chop the carrots, Brussels sprouts, sweet potatoes and 1 red onion and roast them on 2 sheet pans for 25 to 30 minutes, swapping the pans halfway.
Cook 2 cups of rice and stir in the black beans, lime and cilantro.
Slice the other red onion thin and pour the warm pickling brine over it. Stir the chipotle crema together.
Turn the oven down to 375°F. Mix the breakfast bake with 2 cups of the roasted roots and bake it 30 minutes.
Mix 2 jars of gingerbread oats. Air-fry 6 eggs at 270°F for 15 minutes.
Shred the pork in its juices and portion it: 2 for bowls, 2 for tacos, 2 for soup, 2 for Cuban sandwiches in the fridge.
Freeze 1 portion for Christmas Eve nachos. Cooked pork keeps 3 to 4 days, so Thursday's waits in the freezer.
Pack 2 mojo bowls. Keep the crema and pickled onions in jars.

prep.title: Wednesday night
prep.makes: Cuban sandwiches for two and nachos ready for Christmas Eve
steps: Move the frozen pork portion to the fridge.
Press the Cuban sandwiches in the cast iron and warm the roasted roots alongside.

mojo-pork.name: Crock-pot mojo pork

ingredients.qty: 4.5 lb, trimmed of the thick fat

steps: Rub the pork all over with 2½ tsp salt, 1 tsp black pepper, 2 tsp ground cumin and 2 tsp dried oregano.
Lay the sliced onion and 8 smashed garlic cloves in the crock pot, set the pork on top and pour the juice of 2 oranges and 2 limes over it.
Cook on low 8 hours or high 5, until it falls apart.
Shred with two forks, skim the fat off the juices and stir the meat back into them.
Portion into 9 containers of about 1 cup. Fridge 8, freeze 1.
mojo-pork.tip: Cuban-style citrus and garlic pork. It goes bright in bowls and tacos, cozy in soup and rich in a pressed sandwich.

roast-roots.name: Two-tray roasted roots and Brussels sprouts
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the carrots, Brussels sprouts, sweet potatoes and red onion with 3 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1 tsp dried rosemary, 1½ tsp salt and ½ tsp black pepper.
Spread it over 2 sheet pans, Brussels sprouts cut side down.
Roast 25 to 30 minutes, swapping the pans halfway, until the sprouts are deeply browned.
Cool, then store in one big container.
roast-roots.tip: Cut side down is what makes the Brussels sprouts crisp and sweet instead of soggy.

rice-beans.name: Cilantro lime rice and black beans
steps: Cook 2 cups rice in water as the bag directs, with 1½ tsp salt and 1 tbsp olive oil.
Warm the rinsed black beans and fold them in with the zest and juice of 1 lime and the chopped cilantro.
Cool and store. It keeps 5 days.

chipotle-crema.name: Chipotle yogurt crema
steps: Stir 1 cup Greek yogurt, 1 minced chipotle pepper, 1 tbsp of its adobo sauce, the juice of ½ lime, ½ tsp salt and 1 tbsp water together.
Taste and add more adobo sauce if you want it hotter. Freeze the rest of the can in a small bag.

pickled-onions.name: Quick pickled red onions
steps: Pack the thin-sliced red onion into a jar.
Warm ½ cup apple cider vinegar, ½ cup water, 1 tbsp honey and 1 tsp salt until it dissolves and pour it over.
Ready in 30 minutes. Keeps 2 weeks in the fridge.
pickled-onions.tip: They turn bright pink and make every bowl, taco and sandwich taste finished.

egg-bake.name: Roasted veggie breakfast bake
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and spray the pan with cooking spray.
Whisk the 10 eggs, ½ cup milk, ¾ tsp salt and ½ tsp black pepper.
Scatter the chopped roasted roots and spinach in the pan, pour the eggs over and top with ½ cup cheddar and ¼ cup parmesan.
Bake 28 to 32 minutes, until the center is just set.
Cool, cut into 4 and refrigerate. Reheat 60 seconds.
egg-bake.tip: Three breakfasts this week plus a spare square for a snack.

gingerbread-oats.name: Gingerbread overnight oats
steps: Stir 1 cup milk, 1 cup yogurt, 2 tbsp honey, 1 tsp ground ginger, 1 tsp ground cinnamon, a pinch of ground nutmeg and a pinch of salt together.
Stir in 1 cup oats and 3 tbsp raisins and split across 2 jars.
Keeps 4 days. It tastes like a gingerbread cookie, cold or warm.

hb-eggs.name: Air-fryer hard-boiled eggs
steps: Put the eggs straight into the air fryer basket.
Cook at 270°F for 15 minutes.
Move them to a bowl of ice water for 5 minutes, then refrigerate.
Peel and sprinkle with salt to eat.

mojo-bowl.name: Mojo pork rice bowl
steps: Pack rice and beans, roasted roots and pork in each container.
Reheat 2 minutes.
Top with the crema, pickled onions and cilantro.

mojo-tacos.name: Mojo pork tacos with chipotle crema
steps: Crisp both portions of pork in a hot dry cast iron for 4 minutes without stirring, so the edges caramelize.
Warm 6 tortillas in the same pan.
Fill them with half the pork, 1 cup coleslaw mix, pickled onions, half the crema and cilantro, with lime wedges to squeeze.
Pack the rest of the pork over 1 cup rice and beans with the other 1 cup coleslaw mix and the rest of the crema for Wednesday's lunch.
mojo-tacos.tip: Crisping the pork in a dry pan is the difference between good and great.

pork-bean-soup.name: Pork, white bean and kale soup
steps: Soften the diced onion and carrots in 1 tbsp olive oil for 6 minutes, then add the garlic, 1½ tsp Italian seasoning and a pinch of red pepper flakes for 30 seconds.
Add 2¾ cups broth, 1 cup water, the diced tomatoes and the cannellini beans and simmer 10 minutes. Mash a few beans against the pot to thicken it.
Stir in the pork and kale and simmer 3 minutes more.
Top with parmesan. Pack 2 bowls for Thursday and Friday.
pork-bean-soup.tip: Quick enough for after Tuesday pickleball, and it gets better by Thursday.

cuban-sandwich.name: Pressed Cuban sandwiches with roasted roots
cuban-sandwich.equip: cast iron and a heavy pan

ingredients.qty: the loaf, split into 2 long pieces

steps: Warm the pork in the microwave for 1 minute.
Split the French bread loaf into 2 long pieces. Spread 2 tbsp yellow mustard over the cut sides, then layer 3 slices of Swiss, the pork, pickle chips and 3 more slices of Swiss.
Spray the cast iron with cooking spray and set it over medium. Lay in the sandwiches and press them with a heavy pan.
Cook 3 to 4 minutes a side until golden and the cheese melts.
Cut on the diagonal and serve with the roasted roots, warmed in the oven or air fryer.
cuban-sandwich.tip: Dinner for two the night before Christmas Eve. The heavy pan on top is what makes it a real Cubano.

pork-nachos.name: Christmas Eve sheet-pan nachos
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F.
Spread the tortilla chips on a sheet pan and top with the thawed pork, ½ cup rice and beans, the diced red bell pepper and ½ cup cheddar.
Bake 6 to 8 minutes until the cheese bubbles.
Finish with 3 tbsp crema, pickled onions and cilantro.
pork-nachos.tip: A festive 15 minutes after pickleball on Christmas Eve.

cranberry-chicken.name: Cranberry balsamic chicken with herbed couscous
steps: Season the chicken thighs with 1 tsp salt, ½ tsp black pepper and 1 tsp dried rosemary. Sear them in 1 tbsp olive oil in the cast iron, 5 minutes a side, then set them aside.

Add the minced garlic, the whole bag of fresh cranberries, ¼ cup balsamic vinegar, 3 tbsp honey and ¼ cup water to the pan. Simmer 6 to 8 minutes until the berries burst into a glossy cranberry sauce.
Nestle the chicken back in, spoon sauce over and simmer 5 minutes until it reaches 165°F.
Meanwhile, bring 1¼ cups broth to a boil, stir in the couscous, cover off the heat 5 minutes and fluff with parsley and the clementine zest and juice.
Serve over couscous with the roasted roots, warmed in the microwave. Pack one plate for Saturday.
cranberry-chicken.tip: This week's new one: a Christmas dinner that takes 35 minutes. The cranberries cook down into their own jammy sauce.
